st: Grind the hazelnuts in a food processor into a fine meal.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] milk with [[0.25 cup]] sugar until steaming. Whisk the yolks with [[0.25 cup]] sugar in a bowl.
Slowly pour the hot milk into the yolks, whisking. Return to the pot and cook on low for 4 minutes, stirring, until it coats a spoon.
Off the heat, stir in [[8 oz]] chocolate until melted, then [[0.5 cup]] butter and [[1 tsp]] vanilla.
Fold in the ground hazelnuts and cool the filling to spreadable, about 20 minutes.
Whip [[0.75 cup]] cream to soft peaks and fold into the cooled filling.
Stack the wafers, spreading a thin layer of filling between each, with the filling on top and sides.
Press gently under a plate and chill 4 hours.
Cut into small slices with a hot knife.
Mix [[3 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] baking soda in a bowl.
Work in [[0.25 cup]] lard with your fingers until crumbly.
Add [[0.5 cup]] milk and [[0.25 cup]] warm water and knead 5 minutes into a smooth dough.
Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls and roll each into a thin round about 8 inches.
Heat a dry skillet or griddle on medium-high. Cook each round 1 to 2 minutes per side until brown spots show.
Prick any big bubbles with a fork while cooking.
Fill each warm piadina with prosciutto, soft cheese and arugula and fold in half.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] olive oil with the garlic, add [[2 cup]] crushed tomatoes and salt, and simmer 15 minutes.
Melt [[4 tbsp]] butter, whisk in [[4 tbsp]] flour for 1 minute, then pour in [[2.5 cup]] milk slowly, whisking, until thick, 6 minutes.
Season the white sauce with nutmeg and salt.
Boil the pasta sheets for 2 minutes, drain, and lay flat on a towel.
Top each sheet with ham, mozzarella and a spoon of white sauce.
Roll each up and cut into 2-inch spirals, like little nests.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Spread tomato sauce in a baking dish and set the nests in, cut side up.
Top with the rest of the white sauce and [[0.5 cup]] Parmesan. Bake 25 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-inch round pan.
Soak the raisins in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Whisk the eggs with [[0.33 cup]] honey and [[3 tbsp]] oil.
Whisk in [[1.5 cup]] milk.
Mix [[1 cup]] cornmeal, [[1 cup]] flour, [[2 tsp]] baking powder and [[0.25 tsp]] salt, then stir into the wet mix.
Fold in the apples, raisins and [[1 tsp]] lemon zest.
Pour into the pan and bake 45 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 15 minutes before slicing.
Blanch the pork rind in boiling water for 10 minutes, drain, and rinse.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a pot and cook the onion, celery and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add the pork rind, drained beans, bay leaf and [[6 cup]] water.
Bring to a boil, boil hard for 10 minutes, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Simmer partly covered for 90 minutes until the beans are tender, topping up water if needed.
Stir in [[1 cup]] crushed tomatoes and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and cook 30 minutes more.
Season with salt and serve with bread.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C) and boil a kettle of water.
Cook [[0.33 cup]] sugar with [[2 tbsp]] water in a pan until amber, about 6 minutes.
Pour the caramel into a loaf pan or 6 ramekins and tilt to coat the bottom.
Warm [[2 cup]] milk with the lemon zest until steaming, then turn off the heat for 10 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, yolks and [[0.4 cup]] sugar in a bowl, then slowly whisk in the warm milk and [[1 tsp]] vanilla.
Strain into the caramel pan.
Set in a larger pan and pour hot water halfway up the sides. Bake 45 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
Cool, then chill 2 hours before turning out.
